to.title: Shadow: Google reduces Broadcom custom TPU/ASIC orders
to.statement: Unconfirmed report (The Information, anonymous sources, tier 3, 2026-09-11) that Google may reduce Broadcom custom TPU/ASIC orders as it expands in-house silicon. If confirmed, this would cut custom AI silicon revenue from a top customer, directly materializing the in-house-silicon risk flagged in the hyperscaler concentration driver and pressuring the guided AI semiconductor ramp (Q4 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue guided to $21.7B, +236% YoY).
confirmation_triggers: Google or Broadcom confirms/denies order changes or the design relationship
Customer-concentration disclosure in 10-K/10-Q (any single customer >10% of revenue)
Reporting on next-generation TPU design wins or losses
disconfirmation_triggers: Broadcom reiterates AI semiconductor guidance including the Google-related pipeline
A Google-Broadcom next-generation TPU agreement is reported
to.valuation_impact_if_confirmed: Lower AI semiconductor revenue trajectory and likely multiple compression; magnitude cannot be sized without Google's revenue share, which is not disclosed in available evidence.

proposals.reason: A rumor requires verification and quantification before any state or claim change; the Brain currently lacks customer-level revenue data for Google, so this question gates whether the shadow state is promoted, revised, or discarded.

to.question: What share of Broadcom's AI semiconductor (custom ASIC/TPU) revenue comes from Google, and what is the current status of the Google-Broadcom TPU design relationship, including next-generation design wins?
to.reason: The rumored order reduction cannot be sized without Google's revenue share and design pipeline status; customer-level revenue and concentration ratios are not disclosed in the available evidence, leaving the exposure central to the thesis but unmeasured.

proposals.reason: Counter-evidence already in the Brain shows unconfirmed/secondary hyperscaler-silicon news moved AVGO 3.9% (Marvell award). Tracking this rumor's market traction helps interpret price action without asserting the rumor as fact.
